summary.text: The holy Archangel Gabriel is God’s messenger in Daniel and Luke and announces the Incarnation to the Theotokos.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

saints.context: The source’s received ecclesiastical narrative is identified as such. Uncertain dates, later traditions and unknown circumstances of death are retained as uncertain.

blocks.text: Gabriel is an angelic servant of God rather than a human bishop, monk or martyr. Daniel names him when he is sent to explain a vision and again when he comes with understanding concerning the prophet’s prayer. The account presents his authority as received from God.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: Luke identifies Gabriel as the messenger who announces the birth of St. John the Baptist to the priest in the Temple. He then comes to Nazareth and announces to the Virgin Mary that she will bear Jesus, the Son of the Most High. His explanation of the Holy Spirit’s work belongs to the Gospel narrative of the Incarnation.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: A human birth date and death narrative do not apply to this profile. The biblical passages identify Gabriel as a heavenly messenger, so he should not be assigned a martyrdom, burial place or human succession.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The OCA celebrates Gabriel’s Synaxis on March 26, immediately after the Annunciation, and also lists July 13. He is included with the heavenly powers on November 8. A synaxis is a liturgical assembly or commemoration; these observances honor God’s messenger in connection with the saving events he announces.
